name: poisoning-wbtc-68m-flagged-lookalike
why: Verified live on 2026-09-30 ~20:00Z (use ctx.now = 2026-09-30T20:00:00Z). Real incident of 2024-05-03 (~68M USD in WBTC). The calldata is byte for byte that of the theft (tx 0x3374abc5...: WBTC.transfer(0xd9A1C3788D81257612E2581A6ea0aDa244853a91, 115528802767 = 1155.28802767 WBTC)). Victim 0x1E227979...8FD5 history on Blockscout: 09:14:47Z real send of 0.05 ETH to the legitimate 0xd9A1b0B1e1aE382DbDc898Ea68012FfcB2853a91 (tx 0xb18ab131...; shows up in /transactions, NOT in /token-transfers); 09:17:35Z FAKE Transfer event from a spoof 'ETH' token (0x739352337C902c3874B95f14e81ebBCF1B7b262E, method 0xe19c2253, tx sent by the attacker) showing victim->poisoned; 09:17:59Z 0 ETH tx poisoned->victim (0x87c6e5d5...). The poisoned and the legitimate address share the first 4 ('d9a1') and last 4 ('3a91') hex, compared in lowercase. Spec §2 RED rules: 'poisoning detected' (destination differs from the legitimate prior counterparty but has the same prefix/suffix; its first appearance in the history is spoof/0-value); 'GoPlus flag': phishing_activities='1' (data_source SlowMist); 'Blockscout flag': is_scam=true, reputation='scam', metadata tag 'Fake_Phishing327990'. NOTE: eth_simulateV1 at latest REVERTS (the victim no longer has WBTC); the red does not depend on the simulation. Candidate for 'Try a real scam'.
